blocks.heading: Your role
blocks.text: Host a museum gala and lead the investigation into Grant Larceny’s death. You can play too: the murderer is chosen by a secret memorized animal draw, and this guide reveals no character’s private branch.

blocks.heading: Object of the game
blocks.text: Before Coming Clean, identify the murderer and connect their motive with the salon, cabinet key and linen evidence. Guests can read every question and answer directly from their own packet; acting is optional.

blocks.heading: Party details
blocks.text: October 30, 2026 / 1537 S 74th East Ave, Tulsa, OK 74112. Plan 6:00 arrival to 9:30 finish. Assign the first 15 roles before adding more guests. Every attending character can be the murderer.

blocks.heading: One week before
bullets: Assign character names and send each guest only their public introduction PDF or PNG and invitation.
Ask guests to remember their character names. Nobody needs a character number or a partner. Costume ideas are optional.
Read this guide and choose who will deliver the investigation announcements. If playing, keep private packet pages and organizer sources unread.
Choose rooms for the museum labels and print one complete packet per attending guest.

blocks.heading: Before guests arrive
bullets: Staple each twelve-page packet in order. Put a pencil and named place card with it. The ballot and Coming Clean are already inside.
Print the host name checklist. Put the five reports F1–F5 in order in a host folder.
Hide Discoveries 1–16 using page 8. Set an Evidence Table.
Prepare Player Bowl A and matching Murderer Bowl B using all 30 familiar animals, plus one closed return box.
Lower the music for questioning. Guests may sit anywhere; no partner assignment is needed.

blocks.heading: Printing
blocks.text: Single-sided, Actual size / 100%. Staple packets. No font installation is needed. Use a non-playing helper if your printer exposes private text. No player question catalog, evidence-letter cards or finale envelopes are required.

blocks.heading: Assign by personality
blocks.text: Assign the first fifteen names before adding the remaining roles. Names are how guests choose questions and vote. Animals are drawn privately at arrival; every attending role is eligible.

blocks.heading: At arrival
bullets: Each guest draws one animal from Bowl A, reads silently, memorizes it, folds the slip and immediately returns it to the closed box. Nobody keeps or shows a slip.
Draw only from Bowl A. Never put returned slips back into A during arrivals.
When all expected guests have drawn, remove from matching Bowl B every unused animal left in A. B now contains exactly the animals memorized by attending guests.
There is no optional bowl and no name-to-animal list. Keep B separate from the closed return box.

blocks.heading: After Act I
blocks.text: Ask everyone to keep a blank face. Draw one animal from Bowl B and announce it twice. The guest who memorized it uses IF MURDERER; everyone else uses IF INNOCENT. Keep the selected animal in the host folder for the Coming Clean fallback. Do not identify its owner now.

blocks.heading: Late arrivals
blocks.text: A guest arriving after selection may draw an unused A animal and join as innocent: that animal was excluded from B. Before selection, simply include their draw in the normal attendance process.

blocks.heading: One packet per guest
bullets: Print the named SECRET file as one twelve-page packet, face down. Keep pages in order and staple at the left.
Page 1: private background and social tasks. Pages 2–4: Motive. Pages 5–7: Opportunity. Pages 8–10: Method. Page 11: ballot. Page 12: Coming Clean.
Each round has two question pages followed by one answer page. All packets include every target name and the grouped questions.
No cutting or selecting letter cards. No shared question catalog. No separately sealed finale. The final page stays unread until the host calls it.

blocks.heading: Combined printing
blocks.text: If using the combined file, each consecutive twelve-page block is one character’s complete packet. Follow the names on the cover and the public assembly sheet. Never distribute the combined file to guests.

blocks.heading: Host folder
blocks.text: F1–F2 before Motive; F3 before Opportunity; F4–F5 before Method. Keep staged reports separate from the sixteen hidden discoveries.

blocks.heading: When a clue is found
blocks.text: Ask the finder to bring it to the Evidence Table and read it to nearby guests. Record finds for Curator’s Eye. Missing discoveries do not delay the guided investigation.

blocks.heading: Keep the group moving
blocks.text: These are planning allowances, not measured performance times. Read one question and one answer per guest per round. With 30 guests, avoid extra speeches until everyone has answered. Pause for a short discussion after each round.

blocks.heading: Say aloud
blocks.text: Welcome to the Meridian Museum gala. Introduce yourself by your character name, then open only Private background. Your three social tasks are invitations to chat. If a named guest is absent, discuss that subject with anyone. Bring discoveries to the Evidence Table.

blocks.heading: Run Act I
bullets: Invite each guest to give their character name and role. Their public introduction is enough.
Allow mingling, social tasks and discovery hunting. No improvisation or task completion is required to solve the murder.
Ask finders to share the actual document or photograph they found and award one discovery point.
Near the end, gather everyone, turn down the music and announce Grant’s death. Select and announce the murderer animal using page 6.
Say: Read only the current round. Your final Coming Clean page is for after voting.

blocks.heading: Release and announce
blocks.text: Read F1 / Toxicology and F2 / Grant’s unfinished business aloud and display the complete report. Say: Open Motive. Questions are on pages 2–3; your answer is on page 4. Choose by character name, not a number.

blocks.heading: Question chain
bullets: Choose a starting guest. They pick someone who has not answered yet from an ASK row in their packet and read that row’s question.
The named guest reads the appropriate answer box on their Motive answer page, keeping the label private. Several names share a question, but their answers are different.
That guest becomes the next asker and chooses another unanswered person by name. No seating order or partner assignment.
Tick each respondent’s name on the checklist. The starting guest must answer too; have the final respondent ask them if needed.
Ignore absent names. If someone chooses a guest already heard, quietly offer an unanswered name from the same question pages.
When every guest has answered once, stop the chain and invite a short discussion. Then announce Opportunity.

blocks.heading: If a guest needs help
blocks.text: A neighbour may read only the box the guest points to. Do not ask which branch they selected. For Method, the preparation record is inside the answer box and is read aloud with it.

blocks.heading: Collect and lock ballots
bullets: Ask everyone to complete page 11 privately: one accused character, motive and evidence, plus award votes. The murderer votes too.
Collect every ballot before anyone opens Coming Clean. No votes change after collection.

Tally by character name. Select the three highest positive vote totals, or fewer if fewer names received votes. Break equal totals alphabetically by full character name, so there are at most three suspects.

Read the three names aloud in descending vote order. Call each one to read only their IF INNOCENT or IF MURDERER Coming Clean box on page 12. All three get their statement, even if a confession is heard early.

blocks.heading: If nobody confesses
blocks.text: Say: The murderer is not among our three suspects. Whoever memorized [selected animal], please stand and read your IF MURDERER Coming Clean confession. Do not call the animal if one of the three already confessed.

blocks.heading: Award and finish
blocks.text: Master Sleuth: correct murderer, motive and a coherent salon/key/linen explanation. Share equally strong detective awards. Escaped Justice: murderer outside the top three. Use ballot votes for Best Actor and Best Costume; discovery tally for Curator’s Eye. Then debrief over dessert.

blocks.heading: Recovery
bullets: Forgotten animal before selection: restart the draw for everyone. No identity list and no guessing.
Forgotten animal after selection: pause; never guess the murderer. Restart assignments only if all guests can do so, otherwise postpone scoring.
Absent guest: skip their name. Remove their unused animal from B before selection.
Duplicate target: offer an unanswered name. If the chain loses track, the host may ask an unanswered guest directly from the same printed group questions.
Reading ahead: stop before Coming Clean is read aloud. Return to the current round; page 12 opens only after ballots are collected.
Missing packet page: replace the complete named packet. Do not hand a guest a standalone branch.
